clue.text: President presents line of trees in slow motion

parts.note: a wood is a stand of trees

indicators.note: things in motion are moving about, so the letters before this word are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a row is a line; read as a row of wood, a line of trees
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone presents a row of trees filmed in slow motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split as WOODROW from line of trees and WILSON from the shuffled letters of 'in slow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodrow Wilson was the twenty-eighth occupant of the White House, leading America through the First World War.

clue.text: The West Indian politician is a feeble fellow

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
I is the abbreviation for Indian
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Caribbean politician is mocked as a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is an informal term for a timid, weak or ineffectual man.

clue.text: Ex-Tory supply clerk — I belt out one of the BEF

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: something put out of shape is no longer in its usual order, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative
a temp is a clerk supplied for a short spell
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A former Conservative working as a temp clerk lashes out, as if at war.
explanation.walkthrough: The BEF was the British Expeditionary Force of 1914; the Kaiser reputedly called it a 'contemptible little army', and its veterans adopted the name with pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Contemptibles were the regular soldiers of the British Expeditionary Force sent to France in 1914, so each was a member.

clue.text: Make another arrangement for holiday destination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., put in order again
second meaning: a place people go for holidays

explanation.surface: Rebooking a holiday because plans have changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-sort it means arrange again; as a noun it is a popular seaside or ski place for vacations.

clue.text: Colourless boy, probably a criminal

parts.note: wan means pale
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pale lad looks like a likely crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wanted by the police is sought for questioning, and is therefore likely to be an offender.

clue.text: Montefiore forbidden to give horse its dinner?

definitions.note: a noun defined by what it does

parts.note: no as in not allowed
the historian Simon Sebag Montefiore

explanation.surface: Someone called Montefiore is banned from feeding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The historian's full name is Simon Sebag Montefiore, so his middle name stands in for the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feeding bag hung over a horse's head, holding its oats or fodder.

clue.text: Being shown at present: danger arising and I'm not surprised!

parts.note: now means at present
a film or show that is on is being shown

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word danger is read from the bottom up

parts.note: red is the colour of danger

explanation.surface: A threat appears on screen right now, and nobody is startled.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom expressing that something was only to be expected.

clue.text: Beast carries a child according to the time of year

definitions.text: according to the time of year

indicators.note: a creature that carries something holds it inside, so the beast's word wraps the others

parts.note: a seal is an animal
taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An animal carries its young at a set point in the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal describes something that varies with or depends on spring, summer, autumn or winter.

clue.text: Gordon, followed by Frank, strangely, is set to find building land

parts.note: Gordon Brown, Labour Chancellor and later Prime Minister

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: Frank Field, Labour MP for Birkenhead
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two Labour politicians seem poised to locate land for development.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown and Frank Field were Labour politicians of the time; 'Frank' looks like an adjective but is a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownfield sites are previously developed plots, typically old industrial ground, earmarked for new housing or construction.

clue.text: There's glitter as she rings off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's phone calls end amid sparkle and show.
explanation.definitionFit: Garishness is gaudy, showy brightness, the tawdry sparkle loosely called glitter.

clue.text: A touch of the Cretan summit?

parts.note: Mt Ida is the highest mountain on Crete, giving M for Mount plus IDA
read with 'of the' as a possessive: the summit's

explanation.surface: A hint of the peak of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A touch of the Cretan summit' is read as Mt Ida's touch: M + IDA + S. The phrase 'the Midas touch' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: King Midas turned everything he handled to gold, so 'the Midas touch' is the proverbial gift for making money.

clue.text: Another Blair babe on the way?

definitions.text: Another Blair babe on the way?

parts.words: Another Blair babe on the way?
parts.note: surface reading: the Blairs expecting another baby
setter's reading: a fresh childbirth, and also the name of Tony Blair's rebranded party

explanation.walkthrough: Cherie Blair gave birth to Leo in 2000 while Tony Blair was Prime Minister; the answer is both a fresh confinement and his party's slogan name.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is childbirth, so another birth would be a further confinement, and the phrase also names Blair's political movement.

clue.text: 1 19's plan for 12, a round within Hague's capacity

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: William Hague, Tory leader, boasted of drinking fourteen pints a day as a youth
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A president's peace plan seems to hinge on a drinks round and a politician's thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 19 is WOODROW WILSON and 12 is VERSAILLES, the peace conference of 1919. William Hague, then Conservative leader, claimed he once drank fourteen pints a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilson's Fourteen Points of 1918 were his programme for the post-war settlement negotiated at the Paris conference.

clue.text: Palace's following of vice: dispose of one on the way up

parts.note: in 'vice versa' the word that follows vice

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters of the selling phrase are read bottom to top

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A palace is following a path of vice and selling itself off.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the vast royal residence built by Louis XIV outside Paris, where the 1919 treaty was signed.

clue.text: Makes 'ot food

parts.note: makes hot means warms up; the apostrophe in 'ot shows the H is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone warms up the grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ot is hot with a dropped H, so the word for makes hot loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal plural noun for grub or something to eat.

clue.text: One of the family? That would be telling

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the act of narrating a story

explanation.surface: Revealing a family member's identity would give the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a kinsman, and also an account or narration, as in the relation of events.

clue.text: Day when giant nearly reached the Eastern region

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the end of the giant's name is cut short

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
the Philistine giant slain by David

explanation.surface: On a certain day a giant almost made it to the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'nearly' removes the last two letters of the giant's name, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolia is a vast country of Central and East Asia, lying between Russia and China.

clue.text: Araucaria's space poem, "The bird with big feet"

parts.note: the setter refers to himself
a gap is a space
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: The setter announces a space-age poem with a bird title.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the setter, so his name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Megapodes are Australasian mound-building fowl whose name literally means great-footed in Greek.

clue.text: Canterbury pilgrim continuing in the season

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word sits within the season's word

parts.note: summer is a season
on as in carrying on

explanation.surface: A pilgrim to Canterbury keeps going through the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: The Summoner is one of Chaucer's pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Summoner is a church court officer who travels in the company of pilgrims and tells a tale.

clue.text: A left hand writing for the present

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
MS is a manuscript, something written by hand

explanation.surface: A left-handed writer for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand writing' is read as writing by hand, a manuscript, rather than penmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are charitable donations of money or food given to the poor, a gift.

clue.text: See 1 across
Song from Iolanthe (music by Sullivan)

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the operetta's title and the next word

explanation.surface: A number from the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta Iolanthe.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral composition or rousing hymn, such as a national one.

clue.text: Europhile, perhaps, is tottering in a shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so these letters are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pro-European is wobbling amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'a shambles' is both part of the fodder and of the phrase; take the indicator as 'shambles' with 'a' among the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An integrationist favours closer union, and a Europhile backing deeper EU unity is one example.

clue.text: How do you put something between gold and myrrh?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in this way, so
second meaning: frankincense, the gift listed between gold and myrrh

explanation.walkthrough: Thus is an old word for frankincense, the Magi's gift named between gold and myrrh.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this manner, and the noun is a dated name for frankincense resin.

clue.text: Defamatory address to America on line with one phone call

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another comes after it, so the address is placed last

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
Roman numeral one
to give someone a bell is to phone them
O is the vocative of address, as in 'O America', plus US

explanation.surface: A slanderous speech to the American people, delivered by phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give me a bell' is British slang for a phone call. 'On' tells you the address follows the rest in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Libellous means making false, damaging statements in writing, the published form of defamation.

clue.text: Plan in shade of doorway

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an opening in a floor, deck or wall

explanation.surface: A plan sketched in the shadow of an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' is also a meaning: to hatch is to shade a drawing with fine lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To hatch is to devise a scheme, and a hatch is a small door or opening, as on a ship.

clue.text: Loss of moisture — v.p.

parts.note: v. is vide, Latin for see
p. is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A vice-president is losing his juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'v.p.' looks like vice-president but is the reference 'vide page': see page.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through pores or cracks, a gradual leak.

clue.text: Retribution seems in doubt

indicators.note: something in doubt is unsettled, so these letters are not in fixed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Whether justice will come seems uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is deserved downfall or vengeance, named after the Greek goddess of divine punishment.
